title: Headcount phasing decision tree & price sensitivity notes (Q3 2026)
summary: Working worksheet to align hiring phasing with pricing sensitivity scenarios. Combines a compact P&L-like monthly snapshot (tokens, revenue, GPU ops, comp) with a decision tree that triggers hiring accelerations, freezes, or reprice actions based on demand and competitor pressure.

decision_tree_steps: A. Demand trigger: if monthly token growth >15% for two consecutive months -> evaluate moving 50% of Q4 hires forward to Q3 and provision +25% GPU burst capacity.
B. Margin trigger: if gross margin falls below 40% in base pricing -> pause non-critical hires (Solutions Eng, Finance) and run a 10% price increase experiment on new users.

C. Competitor price compression: if competitor list price is >= 20% cheaper and we lose churned customers > 0.8% MoM -> implement fallback model routing (target 20% of traffic) and initiate hiring freeze until impact analysis complete.

D. Enterprise commitments: if signed enterprise ARR >= $300k before Nov 1 -> accelerate Sales AE hires to capture committed pipeline and allocate 2 additional ML infra hires to support on-prem deployments.
E. GPU ops shock: if spot GPU prices increase >40% month-over-month -> enable quantization profile v2 and reduce batching latency targets to reclaim margin; re-evaluate SRE hires.

F. Early-warning monitor: track 5 signals (token growth, gross margin, enterprise signings, GPU ops/hr, churn %) and map each to a binary gate; two or more gates tripped -> convene hiring council within 72 hours.
assumptions: Base price per 1k tokens assumes existing mix (embedding / completion). Hosted API mix is 75% completion, 25% embeddings. GPU ops cost scales roughly linearly with token volume in the short term; quantization adoption reduces ops cost by ~18% at medium adoption and ~32% at high adoption. All comp numbers are fully-burdened (salary + benefits + payroll taxes). Runway calcs assume current cash balance and committed ARR in Confluence page INF-4321.
sensitivity_notes: 1) A -10% price shock reduces revenue in the base case by ~$375k/mo and makes the aggressive hiring plan unaffordable without cutting GPU ops or delaying hires.
2) Improving batching/latency (move from conservative->balanced) reduces GPU ops cost ~12% and can buy back 2-3 hires in the next 6 months.
3) Enterprise deals materially change the headcount ROI curve; one $300k ARR deal covers ~1.5 FTE fully-burdened comp annually.
4) Quantization migration has implementation risk; plan for a 6-week rollout window with 10% temporary latency degradation.
